children: rose about 6% in the afternoon trading on Thursday after The New York Times reported that A24, Sony Pictures Entertainment
were among parties interested in acquiring Letterboxd, valuing the film-focused social network at more than $300 million.
Letterboxd's owners had held early discussions with several potential buyers, including Netflix
co-founder Alexis Ohanian was also reported to be evaluating a potential purchase.

As per the report, several suitors had submitted expressions of interest and that the deal could value Letterboxd at more than $300 million, or about 20 times its projected 2026 earnings of roughly $15 million.
, which acquired a 60% stake in Letterboxd in 2023 in a transaction valued at more than $50 million, has hired investment bank LionTree to explore a sale of a controlling stake.

Letterboxd, founded in 2011, has grown to about 30 million users from 1.8 million in 2020. The platform generates revenue through subscriptions and advertising, with its Pro plan priced at $19 a year and Patron membership at $49.
A potential acquisition would give buyers access to Letterboxd's highly engaged movie-focused audience. Sony
operates Crunchyroll, while A24 has its AAA24 membership program and the New York Times
has a large subscription base across its products.

The report also noted potential challenges for strategic buyers, including preserving Letterboxd's independent identity and managing possible conflicts between the platform and the buyers' existing film businesses.

title: Letterboxd valued at over $300M as buyers circle
